tip: próprio agrees with its noun for 'own': próprias roupas (feminine plural). Masculine would be próprios.
trazer (to bring) is irregular: eu trago, ele traz. Here traz = brings.
Use jogar for sports and games: jogam vôlei. Musical instruments take tocar instead.
trocar means to swap or exchange: troco ideias com os colegas = I trade ideas with them.
Portuguese often uses com + noun where English uses an -ly adverb: com paciência = patiently.
a gente means 'we' but takes the he/she verb form: a gente aluga, not alugamos.
Portuguese has an allergy rather than being allergic: tenho alergia a camarão = I'm allergic to shrimp.
In Brazil chegar (to arrive) takes em: chego na rodoviária. Formal or European usage prefers chegar a.
Questions need no 'do': just keep the verb. Quando abre a padaria? = When does the bakery open?
estar com + noun describes how you feel: estou com preguiça = I feel lazy. Also com fome, com sono.
passar means to spend time: passar as férias = to spend the vacation. Spending money uses gastar.
fui is the preterite of both ir and ser. Here fui à praia = I went; context tells the two apart.
Tô is casual shorthand for estou: Eu tô na correria = I'm in a rush. Spoken, not written.
que (that) can't be dropped: notei que ele estava = I noticed [that] he was. English can omit it.
porque, one word with no accent, means 'because': abri a janela porque = I opened it because.
soube is the preterite of saber and means found out or realized, not 'knew': a gente soube na hora.
tomar banho = to take a shower. tomar (to take) is the verb for showers and drinks: tomava banho.
